Definition: from δαίω (to distribute fortunes); a dæmon or supernatural spirit (of a bad nature):--devil.
BiblicalUsage: This is the New Testament word for a demon, a spirit of a bad nature, and it appears once in this exact form, when the devils in the Gadarene demoniacs beg Jesus to send them into the swine. The demons know who He is, and they know He can cast them out.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the demons' fear is instructive: even the spirits of darkness confess Christ's authority, and we should not fear what fears Him.
